title: Does the Short Form Fit the Word
statement:
A short form of a word replaces some runs of its letters with the number of letters skipped. For "keyboard", "k3oa1d" keeps k, skips 3 letters, keeps o and a, skips 1 letter and keeps d.

You get a word and a short form abbr made of lowercase letters and digits. Return true if abbr is a valid short form of word:

  • Letters in abbr must match the word's letters at that point exactly.
  • A run of consecutive digits is one number, and it skips that many letters. It must not have a leading zero, and it cannot be 0.
  • Together, letters and skips must cover the word exactly, with nothing left over on either side.

examples.why: k, skip "eyb", o, a, skip "r", d: every letter accounted for.
07 has a leading zero, which is not allowed even though 7 skips would fit.
The digits 1 and 2 form the single number 12, which runs past the end of the word. Reading them as 1 then 2 would wrongly give a match.

constraints: word has only lowercase letters; abbr has lowercase letters and digits
hints: Walk both strings at once with one index into word and one into abbr. What should each kind of character in abbr do to the word index?
A letter must equal word[i] and moves both indexes by one. A digit starts a number: read all following digits first, then jump the word index by the whole number.
Reject a number that starts with 0. At the end, both indexes must have reached the end of their strings at the same time.

explain.intuition:
Think of abbr as instructions for a cursor moving through word. A letter says "the next letter is this one", a number says "skip ahead this far". You follow the instructions and see whether the cursor lands exactly on the end of the word.

The two traps are in the numbers. Several digits in a row form one number, so you must collect the whole run before skipping. And a number written with a leading zero, including 0 alone, is not a valid skip.
steps: If abbr[j] is a letter: if i is past the end or word[i] ≠ abbr[j], return false; else move both forward.
If it is a digit: if it is 0, return false. Otherwise read digits while they last into a number k, then set i += k.
If i goes past the word length, return false.
pitfalls: Treating each digit as its own skip, so a12e on apple skips 1 then 2 and matches.
Allowing leading zeros or a lone 0.
Forgetting the final check, so "4" on "apple" returns true with one letter never covered.

solutions.title: Split into tokens first
solutions.idea: Cut abbr into letter and number tokens with a regular expression, then replay them against the word.

solutions.title: Two indexes in one pass
solutions.idea: Move a cursor through word as you read abbr; build each number digit by digit.

followups: Given a word, list every valid short form of it. How many are there for a word of length n?
Find the shortest short form of a word that does not also fit any word in a given dictionary.
